title: world premiere musical by the beach? sign me up! @Becca Suskauer @njr...
transcript: if you're a theatre fan in need of a beach escape do I have the perfect spot for you this week I went to New Jersey Rep to catch a beautiful brand new musical and got to spend a few hours taken in the ocean Rebecca and I drove down to the Jersey Shore to see how my grandparents fell in love a world premiere new musical that is deeply romantic very funny and extremely timely it tells the true story of the writer's grandparents Charlie is a Polish born Jew who owns a shoe repair store in America but has returned home looking for a wife he quickly meets chava a shop girl at a hat store who is brilliant. beautiful and has big dreams and is not looking for a husband but sometimes love is just Beshert now full disclosure I found out about this show because Becca Suskauer is a friend of mine but I don't think it's biased at all to tell you that she was made for this role she's an incredible actress and storyteller and her voice with this music was perfect it's a joy getting to watch her tell this story especially opposite Harris Milgrim as Charlie who is so unbelievably charming you just believe them as a couple immediately this show is so sweet and romantic and quietly powerful and I really hope they record the score because I loved the music it's running Thursday through Sundays until August 10th at New Jersey Rep which is by the way an extremely cool theatre they focus entirely on developing new works and in there almost 30 year history have had 125 world premiere shows and I just love that they're bringing new stories to the stage if you get a chance head down to the shore to see how my grandparents fell in love I honestly cannot wait to see where this musical goes next
showTitle: How My Grandparents Fell in Love, A Musical
classificationReason: Creator attended the world premiere at NJ Rep and gives clear first-hand opinions: praises Becca Suskauer as 'made for this role,' calls Harris Milgrim 'unbelievably charming,' and describes the show as 'sweet and romantic and quietly powerful.'
